title: Verifier‑Assisted vs. LLM‑Only Pre‑deployment Network‑Change Validation: A Confirmatory Paired Study
abstract: We measured whether adding a deterministic pre‑deployment verifier (with up to one automated repair) increases the fraction of intent‑driven configuration proposals that pass semantic validation versus accepting a single LLM candidate. Under a preregistered paired design (cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001; preregistration SHA‑256 = 425cb1652354120cf48f686b964723d64c76d0a8abe53cd5b5ad0eaa1af71fc7) we executed 300 paired intents (100 per difficulty stratum) using gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Each pair used one shared LLM generation (shared_initial) that both conditions evaluated: baseline = accept single shot; guarded = validate and permit ≤1 automated repair. Results (analysis/condition_summary.csv): baseline 299/300 unflagged passes (0.9966667), guarded 300/300 (1.0); paired contingency n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; absolute paired difference = 0.0033333; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% paired bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00,0.01] (bootstrap_seed=1729, B=10000). The primary estimand is conditional on the single shared_initial LLM candidate per pair; under the supplied synthetic suite and model the baseline was near ceiling, leaving minimal room for guarded rescue. We archive the frozen preregistration, full execution traces, and the repair provider trace (artifact path and concise redacted excerpt given in Results) and discuss construct/external validity and recommendations for studies under weaker models or more heterogeneous real intents.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed for NetOps tasks such as intent→configuration translation, template synthesis, and automated repair. Prior system and survey work shows that tool augmentation (generate→validate→repair) can reduce syntactic and semantic errors, but reported benefits vary with model quality, task difficulty, and validator coverage. We preregistered and executed a confirmatory paired experiment to quantify the incremental effect of a deterministic verifier (with one automated repair permitted) on an identical LLM candidate per intent. Research question: Does a verifier‑assisted pipeline increase the probability that an LLM candidate passes semantic pre‑deployment validation (unflagged) compared with accepting a single‑shot LLM output when both conditions evaluate the same candidate? Contributions: (1) a preregistered paired evaluation (N=300 pairs) using a shared_initial protocol that isolates verifier+repair effects conditional on the same candidate; (2) artifact‑archived execution and analysis demonstrating a near‑ceiling baseline under the chosen synthetic suite and model; (3) interpretation and recommendations about estimand selection, validator role, and follow‑up study designs.
sections.related_work: Recent surveys and system papers document active research in LLMs for network configuration, intent translation, tool‑augmented agents, and generate→validate→repair architectures. Representative lines of work indicate (a) LLMs can synthesize configuration templates and intent translations, (b) planner‑centric and tool‑augmented frameworks enable verifier/tool calls, and (c) hybrid repair methods often reduce errors compared with unconstrained generation. However, published evaluations vary in task definitions, validator semantics, and scaffolding, leaving open how large a verifier's marginal benefit is under controlled estimands. Our study complements this literature with a preregistered, artifact‑backed paired design that conditions on identical model candidates to measure deterministic rescue/repair utility.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and design: The study preregistration (cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001; SHA‑256 above) specified a paired confirmatory design with 300 analyzable pairs (100 per complexity stratum: low/medium/high), a shared_initial generation per pair, and the primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Key design choices fixed before execution: (a) model: declared gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json); (b) baseline: accept shared_initial output as the final proposal; (c) guarded: run deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (full_intent_constraint_validation) on shared_initial and, if it failed, permit at most one automated repair call followed by revalidation; (d) seed and analysis executors frozen (paired_binary_analysis_v1 implementing exact two‑sided McNemar‑equivalent test and paired bootstrap percentile CI with B=10000 and seed=1729). The shared_initial protocol conditions the estimand on the exact candidate produced once per pair; it isolates the validator/repair effect for that candidate but does not capture benefits that would arise from independent alternative candidate draws per condition. Inclusion/exclusion rules: pairs were excluded only if both calls failed due to provider/infrastructure outage (none occurred). Execution: planned 600 episodes (300 pairs × 2 conditions), completed 600; model_calls_used=301 (shared_initial calls=300; repair calls=1). Analysis: primary confirmatory test produced the contingency (n11,n10,n01,n00) and the absolute paired difference with exact two‑sided p and bootstrap CI. Exact‑test clarification: paired_binary_analysis_v1 uses the standard exact conditional McNemar approach that conditions on total discordants m = n10 + n01 and treats n10 as Binomial(m,0.5); two‑sided p is computed as 2·min{Pr[N ≤ n10], Pr[N ≥ n10]} under Binomial(m,0.5) with truncation to ≤1.0. With m=1 and n10=1 this yields p = 2·min{1.0, 0.5} = 1.0 (see Results).
sections.results: Execution accounting and margins: planned_episode_count=600, completed_episode_count=600, complete_pair_count=300, model_calls_used=301, stage_counts: shared_initial_generation=300, repair=1 (execution_manifest.json; deterministic_reconciliation.json). Condition margins (analysis/condition_summary.csv): baseline successes 299/300 (0.9966667), guarded successes 300/300 (1.0). Paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv): n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0. Confirmatory inference (paired_binary_analysis_v1): absolute paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0033333; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% paired bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00,0.01] (bootstrap_seed=1729, B=10000). Per‑stratum outcomes: baseline — low 100/100, medium 100/100, high 99/100; guarded — 100/100 each (total 300/300). Exact‑test note: the exact two‑sided conditional procedure conditions on m = n10 + n01 = 1 and computes P by the binomial reference; with a single discordant observation all in one direction the two‑sided p equals 1.0, reflecting the paucity of discordant evidence rather than evidence of equality. Archived rescue and artifact pointer: one guarded episode invoked the single allowed automated repair and turned a baseline failure into a guarded pass (the lone discordant, n10=1). The full low‑level repair provider trace for that episode is archived in the run bundle at execution/raw_results.jsonl (sha256 = 2ce4c0074b64a8c9b42ee59d2ea33f4d6af25835f8f5ec42aaa0103382696b32) and is referenced by the execution manifest and reconciliation artifacts. Concise redacted excerpt (semantic summary derived from validator traces and task workflow_policies in the archive): "Automated repair inserted the required 'admin down' sequencing step before a VLAN/MTU field change to satisfy the validator's must_be_down_for_fields workflow policy; after insertion the deterministic validator reported valid == true and the episode scored as a guarded pass." Representative example (from task_manifest): task-000001 intent — "Migrate edge1 to VLAN 30 and MTU 1600. For safety, shut edge1 down before changing either VLAN or MTU, then restore it." Representative scoring artifact excerpts for task-000001 (execution/responses/task-000001-*.txt) and the task_manifest entry are archived and cited in the evidence bundle; they illustrate the task format, required_sequence, and validator trace semantics. Contamination and missingness: analysis/contamination_summary.csv reports no contamination flags; missingness_summary.csv shows no excluded or failed episodes.
sections.discussion: Interpretation: On this synthetic suite with gpt-5-mini, single‑shot generation already satisfied the deterministic validator for 299/300 intents, leaving minimal headroom for the guarded pipeline to demonstrate a large absolute improvement on the shared_initial estimand. The lone guarded‑only rescue demonstrates that deterministic validators can deterministically flag workflow violations and that automated repairs can recover specific ordering errors. However, measured marginality depends strongly on (i) base model capability, (ii) task hardness and validator coverage, and (iii) estimand conditioning (shared_initial vs. independent draws). Threats to validity: internal — design fixed priors, single shared_initial draw per pair, and repair budget (≤1) constrain observed effects; construct — the synthetic generator and deterministic validator share workflow semantics (e.g., must_be_down_for_fields), which may make many intended changes easier than in heterogeneous real networks; external — single model (gpt-5-mini), single validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), and synthetic topologies limit generalisability; conclusion validity — near‑ceiling baseline produced few discordants, reducing inferential power to detect small absolute differences. Operational implications and recommendations: (1) when base models are near‑ceiling on a target validator suite, the incremental benefit of a guard may be small for the shared_initial effect but still valuable for auditing and targeted rescues; (2) to assess end‑to‑end pipeline gains consider independent draws per condition (not shared_initial) or evaluate weaker models/real operator intents to increase discordance; (3) report model call budgets, latency, and repair cost alongside correctness metrics to inform operational tradeoffs.
sections.conclusion: We report a preregistered, artifact‑archived paired comparison of a verifier‑assisted pipeline versus single‑shot LLM generation for pre‑deployment NetOps changes using gpt-5-mini and a deterministic NetOps validator on a synthetic topology suite. Baseline single‑shot generation achieved 299/300 unflagged verifier passes and the guarded pipeline 300/300, producing a negligible paired improvement (0.00333; paired McNemar two‑sided p=1.0; 95% CI [0.00,0.01]). These results illustrate that measurable verifier marginality depends on base model capability, task difficulty, validator coverage, and the chosen estimand (the shared_initial conditional effect). We release full preregistration, execution, and analysis artifacts to facilitate community follow‑up under weaker models and more heterogeneous real‑world conditions.

limitations: Synthetic benchmark: tasks and topologies were generated by the preregistered deterministic task generator; real‑world heterogeneity may expose different failure modes and increase verifier marginal utility.
Single model and validator: only gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 were evaluated; results may not generalize to other LLMs or richer/verifier‑diverse validators.

Ceiling effect: baseline single‑shot performance was near 100% on this suite (299/300), producing limited discordance and low power to detect small absolute improvements relative to the preregistered target (10 percentage points).
Pilot not executed: the preregistered pilot (n=60) intended for discordance estimation and power calibration was not executed; the main N=300 was used as pre‑specified.
Estimand conditioning: the shared_initial protocol conditions the estimand on a single LLM candidate and therefore does not measure verifier benefit when independent LLM draws per condition differ.

Representative repair transcript availability: the archived run bundle contains the low‑level repair provider trace documenting the single automated repair and subsequent validation pass (recorded in execution/raw_results.jsonl and referenced in the execution manifest). The manuscript reports the archive‑traceable semantic summary of that repair in Results rather than reproducing a full verbatim provider transcript in the body.
